short: The charismatic Stuart prince who led the ill-fated 1745 Jacobite rising.
full:
Born in 1720, Charles Edward Stuart, often remembered as "Bonnie Prince Charlie", was the eldest son of the exiled James Francis Edward Stuart. Believing he could succeed where his father had failed, Charles landed in Scotland in July 1745 with minimal resources, relying on his personal charisma and the loyalty of the Highland clans to launch a major rebellion.

He initially achieved stunning success, capturing Edinburgh and marching his army as far south as Derby before being forced to retreat. Following his devastating defeat at Culloden in 1746, he spent months as a fugitive in the Highlands before escaping to Europe. He never returned to Britain, and spent his remaining decades in bitter exile, his cause entirely broken.
